sentences.text:
The petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, to quash Annexure-I Final Report in Crime No.892/2021 of the Nedumangad Police Station and all further proceedings in C.C.
No.16/2022 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court -II, Nedumangad.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court -II, Nedumangad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The petitioners' case is that they are the accused Nos. 1 to 4 in the above crime, which is registered against them for an offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The prosecution allegation against the petitioners is that, the first petitioner is the husband of the defacto complainant - the third respondent.

On 14.1.2018, the first petitioner :: 3 ::
took away the gold ornaments of the third respondent and gave it to the third petitioner for his personal needs.
The petitioners 2 and 4 used to harass the third respondent demanding more dowry.
Hence, they have committed the above offence.
4. Heard; the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, the learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 and the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent.
Perused the materials on record.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that with the intervention of well-wishers and friends, the subject matter in dispute between the petitioners and the third respondent has been settled out of court.

The above submission is endorsed by the learned :: 4 ::
counsel appearing for the third respondent, who submitted that the third respondent has filed Annexure-2 affidavit, inter alia, stating that the dispute between the parties has been settled and the 3rd respondent is no longer desirous of pursuing Annexure-1 as against the petitioners.

Suhair vs State Of Kerala on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153818076/
2 6.

The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the Investigating Officer has ascertained and reported that the dispute between the petitioners and the third respondent has been settled and the third respondent has voluntarily executed Annexure-2 affidavit.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303] and Prabatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and others v. State of Gujarat and another [(2017) 9 SCC 641] has :: 5 ::
held that in the facts and circumstances of a case and to secure the ends of justice,
where the High Court is satisfied that an amicable settlement has been arrived at between the parties and the offence is not serious in nature involving mental depravity, criminal proceedings may be quashed.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Prabatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinhbhai Karmur and others v. State of Gujarat and another [(2017) 9 SCC 641]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. On a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, and on being convinced that ends of justice would justify the exercise of the inherent power of this Court,
particularly since the alleged offences are not serious in nature, no public interest is involved, the chances of conviction is remote, the continuation of the proceeding would only be wastage of judicial time and the settlement would augur harmony, I am satisfied that the petition is to be allowed.
In the result, the Crl.M.C is allowed.

Annexure-1 Final Report in Crime No.892/2021 of the Nedumangad Police Station and all further proceedings in C.C No.16/2022 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Nedumangad, as against the petitioners,

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II, Nedumangad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: are quashed.
The Crl.M.C is ordered accordingly.
